title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: Player TWO fields 5 CAMEL_RIDERs before Vienna; camel cavalry was not a component of the 1529 Ottoman force operating in Lower Austria, and the engine's LIGHT_CAVALRY/CAVALRY_ARCHER (already present) adequately covers sipahis and akinci

The Ottoman infantry are CROSSBOWMAN x6 rather than JANISSARY, an available Turkish gunpowder unit; the janissary corps was the backbone of the assaults on the Carinthian Gate and its omission is avoidable
The defenders' 'Spanish arquebusiers' named in Salm's dialogue are represented by CROSSBOWMAN and SKIRMISHER; HAND_CANNONEER exists in the engine and is the obvious match for 1529 firearms

BATTERING_RAM, MANGONEL and ONAGER as the Ottoman siege train misrepresent a 1529 siege that turned on gunpowder mining and light field guns (Suleiman's heavy artillery was abandoned in the mud); a single BOMBARD_CANNON is the only gunpowder piece placed
Both commanders are generic KING units rather than any distinguishing hero object, so Salm and Suleiman exist only in text

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the defenders may appear with Aztec, Japanese or Mongol architecture and unit skins instead of a Central European (Teutons/Hungarians/Bohemians) garrison and an Eastern (Turks) besieger — an avoidable assignment error given the engine ships a Turks civ explicitly modelled on the Ottomans.
The brief's 'Spanish arquebusiers' are represented by 6 CROSSBOWMAN; the engine ships HAND_CANNONEER, the obvious gunpowder-infantry stand-in for 1529 arquebusiers, so the choice is avoidable.

The Ottoman roster contains no gunpowder infantry at all: janissaries, the core of Suleiman's assault troops at the Carinthian Gate, are absent (again HAND_CANNONEER or ELITE_JANISSARY were available), and the attackers are instead 5 CAMEL_RIDER, 4 LIGHT_CAVALRY and 6 CAVALRY_ARCHER — a steppe/desert cavalry force that did not storm Vienna's breaches.

Ottoman siege train includes BOMBARD_CANNON, MANGONEL and ONAGER; Suleiman's heavy artillery was in fact bogged down and left behind on the Danube march, which is why the siege turned on mining rather than battering — the placed content contradicts the scenario's own mine-centred narrative.
3,541 TREE_OAK dominate the map, making the Vienna plain and its trench/siege lines into dense forest; the historical approaches and Ottoman camp were open ground.
Both commanders are the same generic KING object, so Salm and Suleiman are visually indistinguishable and neither is characterised beyond dialogue.
No sapper/mine visual apparatus beyond a scripted KILL_OBJECT on a wall segment; the countermining the brief foregrounds is narration plus one trigger rather than playable content.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit bonuses and skins for a Habsburg city under Ottoman siege are left to chance; Teutons/Spanish and Turks were both available.

The text promises 'Landsknechts! Arquebusiers!' but the garrison contains no Hand Cannoneers at all — only Crossbowmen and Skirmishers — despite the engine shipping Hand Cannoneer, the obvious 1529 arquebus stand-in. This is an avoidable mismatch between narration and placed content.

The Ottoman roster likewise has no Janissary/Hand Cannoneer element, the most famous component of Suleiman's 1529 army; instead it is dominated by Camel Riders, Light Cavalry and Cavalry Archers, which overstates the mounted share of a siege force.

A Bombard Cannon plus Mangonel/Onager overstates Ottoman siege artillery at Vienna: Suleiman's heavy guns were largely lost or left behind on the muddy march, which is why he relied on mining — the very mechanic the scenario otherwise dramatises.
Defender numbers (3 Champions, 6 Pikemen, 6 Crossbowmen, 4 Skirmishers) are a token garrison for a force of roughly 20,000; acceptable as scale abstraction but no Landsknecht mass is conveyed.
Only one gate and a single 123-tile stone wall circuit; the Carinthian Gate is named only in text, with no distinguishing bastion or earthwork outworks that Salm actually threw up.
